title: add sse preamble sanitize and rescue handler for truncated json tokens
author: Priya Rao
description: Fixes a class of production failures where SSE chunks beginning with non-event preamble or ending with truncated JSON tokens caused the OpenAI-compat streaming adapter and downstream structured-output parsers to lose the following event or emit malformed JSON. This PR introduces a small sanitize-and-rescue layer in the stream framer that: 1) strips noisy preamble characters (control bytes, stray commas/newlines outside of an event), 2) enforces an explicit 'event start' predicate (preamble guard) before handing bytes to the JSON reassembler, 3) detects likely-truncated JSON fragments at chunk boundaries using bracket/quote balance heuristics and a lightweight trailing-token scanner, and 4) exposes a deterministic rescue path that either buffers until a recovery boundary or emits a stable partial object with a sentinel and checksum for consumers to reconcile. Motivation: incidents recorded in ENG-1083 and follow-ups showed multiple customer streams failing when browsers/proxies coalesced or split event boundaries in unexpected places; existing reassembly assumed well-formed chunk boundaries and did not consider stray control preambles injected by some intermediate proxies. Changes are intentionally minimal in surface area to avoid perf regressions: the sanitizer runs a fast byte-scan early; the rescue buffer is bounded and uses a short-circuit checksum to detect self-consistency before passing to JSON decode. The PR also updates the OpenAI-compat adapter to treat the per-event sentinel consistently for function/tool-calling handoffs so that truncated function call payloads never suppress subsequent tool invocation events. Includes unit tests, integration tests against a simulated lossy chunker, and a small e2e harness that replays real incident traces. Checklist: (x) implement sanitizer and rescue logic; (x) add unit tests for bracket/quote heuristics; (x) add integration test with lossy chunker; (x) update adapter to accept sentinel+checksum; (x) update docs for streaming framing; (x) add migration/rollout notes. Runtime impact: measured median pipeline add of ~0.6ms per-chunk on our stress harness; worst-case buffering is constrained by config and defaults to 64KB and 250ms. Rollout: staged canary -> 25% -> 100% with opt-out flag for Dedicated customers provided for first 48h. Related: ENG-1083, ENG-2150, PM-342.

review_comments: Diego Morales: Can you ensure the rescue buffer is bounded per-stream rather than global? We saw a similar OOM in a different change. - addressed in b7e1f02, buffer is per-framer instance and configurable.

Hannah Li: Suggest making the preamble sanitizer tolerant to common proxy patterns, not strict stripping, to avoid dropping benign commas. Consider telemetry for sanitized bytes. - added telemetry and heuristics to only strip non-printable control bytes and stray-leading commas when not inside a record.

Marcus Nguyen: Tests look good; can you add an e2e replay of the production trace that triggered ENG-1083 so we can validate behavior? - added replay harness and included the incident trace in tests/integration under a redacted fixture.
Diego Morales: Approve after small nits fixed in docs and a comment in stream_framer about the 250ms default. - addressed and comments added.
release_notes: Stabilize SSE streaming by sanitizing noisy preambles and adding a bounded rescue path for truncated JSON tokens. Improves resilience of function/tool-calling handoffs in lossy network conditions.
notes: Monitoring added: rescue_count, rescue_latency_ms, sanitized_bytes. Rollout gated by feature flag streaming.rescue_enabled default=true; Dedicated customers can opt-out via support for 48h. Follow up: consider adaptive buffer sizing if rescue_count>threshold in 1h windows.
